steps.message:
# Ship is damaged when performing the action shown in the recording

### What happens
`recording.mp4` shows a ship performing an action at a station. The action does not
go the way it is set up to go, and the ship does not come out of it unharmed.
The collision outlines of the ship and the pad already overlap while the ship sits still, although the video shows it resting clear of the pad. The ship in the video is not the one the game starts you with; work out which ship it is first. A ship that really lands on a pad must still be caught by it, and the ship must keep its overall proportions.

### Expected
Performing the action shown in the recording must not damage the ship at all, at the spot shown in
the video or at any other equivalent spot of the same station. The hull-integrity readout stays at
100% for the whole action.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`

You can inspect the video frame by frame with `ffmpeg` (installed in the image), e.g. extracting
still frames at specific timestamps to look closely at the HUD and the ship.

Inspect the attached file before making changes. The video describes observable behavior; it does
not prescribe source files, internal names, or an implementation strategy.

arguments.command: cd /app; ls; git log --oneline|head; find . -type f -not -path './.git/*' | grep -v node_modules | head -100; ffprobe .harbor_assets/recording.mp4 2>&1 | tail -5

steps.message:
I've changed the collision mesh of the **Mola Ramsayi** freighter. It's the only ship whose collision outline extended into the pad while it was docked. I couldn't watch the recording: `/app/.harbor_assets/` is empty. I worked out which ship it was from the model data, and the game isn't built, so the fix hasn't been tested in-game.

**How I found the ship.** I compared every ship's collision mesh (with its part positions applied) against its visible model and its landing point. Every ship matched except the Mola Ramsayi. Its three rear heat-sink fins are animated with the landing gear:
- **Gear up:** the fins tilt 20° outward.
- **Gear down (sitting on a pad):** they fold to about 6° inward. The visible fins then sit about 1.5 m above the pad.

The collision mesh had the fins fixed in the gear-up position. That put the lower fin tips about 5 cm above the landing surface (Z −7.16 against −7.206). They also stuck out sideways to ±11.4 m, while the visible hull is ±8.26 m wide. So when docked, the ship's collision outline touched the pad even though the ship looked clear of it. Once the ship is released at takeoff, any contact with the pad counts as a crash and damages the hull.

**The fix.** It's one file, `data/models/ships/molaramsayi/molaramsayi_col.dae`. I set the three fin positions in the collision mesh to the gear-down pose of the visible model. I didn't change any engine code, other ships, or stations, so every pad of every station gets the same result.

- **Clear of the pad:** the lowest fin point is now about 1.5 m above the landing surface instead of 5 cm.
- **Still caught by the pad:** the main hull, which is the real contact surface, is unchanged. Its bottom still sits exactly at the landing point (−7.206).
- **Proportions kept:** I didn't scale anything. The collision outline now matches the visible ship: ±8.26 m wide, about 37.4 m long, height −7.21 to 9.10 m.

There's no precompiled model cache that would override the edited file. The change isn't committed.
